description: Verifier/evaluator wire-contract truth table. Each case states an input (the scoped KG obligations, the measurement, and the language model's scripted output) and the externally observable outcome a conforming SKI implementation MUST produce: either an HTTP status (for inputs rejected at the API boundary) or the verdict, the verifier_result.status, and any required verifier_result.divergences substrings. These describe the WIRE contract (what /api/evaluate returns), not any implementation's internals. They encode finding C1 (fail-open verifier) from the 2026-10-09 gold-standard review; the reference runtime enforces every case in conformance/adversarial/test_fail_closed_verifier.py.
notes: A verdict is 'never CLEAR' means the API MUST NOT return verdict == 'CLEAR' for that input at ANY risk tier.
SCHEMA_VIOLATION and OMITTED_OBLIGATION are verifier divergence kinds, surfaced as substrings in verifier_result.divergences; they are not verifier_result.status values.
A SCHEMA_VIOLATION (assertion predicate outside the closed, verifier-checkable set) routes the verdict to DISCRETIONARY at every tier.
Non-finite and non-numeric readings for numeric obligations are rejected at the API boundary with HTTP 422 before any verdict is formed.

cases.rationale: The model asserted only the satisfied nox.cap and omitted the breached so2.cap. The verifier grounds every mapped obligation against the measurement, detects the omitted breach, and refuses CLEAR.
Omitting a SATISFIED obligation is not a violation; the fail-closed verifier must not produce false positives on honest CLEARs.
A junk predicate ('must_be_reasonable') is a SCHEMA_VIOLATION and cannot mask the real breach (observed 150 > 100). LLM_CONTRADICTION wins over UNVERIFIABLE by precedence; the verdict is never CLEAR.

cases.finding: C1(b) masking: schema violation routes to DISCRETIONARY
cases.rationale: Even with the real obligation satisfied, an assertion carrying a predicate outside the closed verifier-checkable set is a SCHEMA_VIOLATION, which routes the verdict to DISCRETIONARY at every tier rather than CLEAR.

A -Infinity reading (which a permissive JSON parser accepts) for a numeric obligation is not a usable sample and is rejected at the API boundary with 422 before any verdict is formed. Same for +Infinity, NaN, and booleans.
With no formalizable subset the verifier is UNVERIFIABLE. A missing or unrecognised risk tier resolves to tier-1 (strictest), at which an unverifiable CLEAR is downgraded to DISCRETIONARY.

cases.finding: C1(c) control: declared tier-2/3 accepts an unverifiable CLEAR
cases.rationale: At an explicitly declared low-criticality tier (tier-3) an unverifiable qualitative CLEAR is accepted. The governor only tightens when the tier is missing or unknown.
